Although these networks are often trained on vast datasets, they frequently fail to achieve robustness because the training data does not accurately reflect real-world environments. We introduce a framework designed to enhance deep networks' generalization and resilience to environmental factors through adaptive networks that process local data contextually. Driven by the hypothesis that scene characteristics differ across time and space, our approach employs a context-dependent modulator that integrates with the main network and a learned context encoder via element-wise multiplication, allowing adaptation of features according to local attributes. Training this model simply by stacking it directly on top of the base classifier and adding its parameters allows it to function as a lightweight heads for various tasks. We validate our method across two applications: classifying images based on scene text description and segmenting them according to scene text attributes, utilizing a large dataset containing over 100 million images tagged with scene descriptions. Results indicate superior generalization and robustness against real-world variations in lighting and weather compared to standard models, particularly when key characteristics fluctuate within an image set.

cling has become an increasingly favored mode of transport in numerous cities. However, a study of Beijing reveals that weather conditions, particularly rain, deter many from cycling even when roads are wet and slippery. This research investigates the safety risks associated with bicycling on wet surfaces by comparing the friction coefficients of bicycle tires against those of car tires under identical wet conditions. Through controlled slip-angle tests using both multi-block rubber sheets and dedicated tires, the Coefficient of Friction (CFC) was measured. Results indicate that the friction coefficients for rubber sheets are comparable to those for car tires, confirming that multi-block technology does not significantly outperform its rivals. Furthermore, the data reveals that bicycle tire CFC is 20% to 40% lower than that of car tires. This substantial disparity highlights the severe safety risks bicyclists face on wet roads, suggesting that safety improvements could be achieved through the integration of effective anti-slip coatings or materials inspired by nature, such as shark skin, alongside public education regarding cycling safety.

While this concern has prompted the neural science community to investigate how such phenomena affect internal representations, this paper specifically targets this gap. We demonstrate that these adversarial attacks severely disrupt the feature learning process in deep networks. Our findings indicate that while clean data allows for consistent feature extraction, these disturbances lead to increasingly divergent learning as the network's depth increases. Second, we present a new regularization approach focused specifically on minimizing the Lipschitz constant, which enhances the model's inherent resistance to adversarial examples.

Despite the fact that the solar minimum is typically associated with the absence of complex magnetic fields, PTMs are unique in this regard. for constructing distributed applications. As distributed applications evolve, the internal architecture changes, often leading to service updates. While automated systems are available to orchestrate these updates, they frequently overlook critical aspects like services relying on internal helper processes or handling client connections across multiple ports. Consequently, applications may enter inconsistent states, causing internal component failures or blocking all incoming service requests. To resolve these issues, application architects, engineers, and developers require strategies to temporarily modify services, allowing them to revert later after handling updates in a way that prevents control flow or data storage leaks during the vulnerable period. General service gating mechanisms, designed to temporarily disconnect services from the network, already exist in the literature. However, standard gating approaches fail to contain the leakage of control flow or data within applications. To address this, this work introduces the Safe-Gate extension to service gating specifically for distributed systems. Our proposed Safe-Gate strategy ensures that services briefly sever connectivity to prevent internal flow leaks while managing service updates.

This work examines how reduced dimensionality affects the three-body recombination of a gas of polar molecules, specifically focusing on the long-range dipolar attraction. We present the formulation of a three-body parameter for systems with long-range potentials, anchored in a two-body scattering length, and validate this approach through exact numerical calculations. By comparing the three-body parameter for different gases and various systems relative to different power-law potentials, we find that the ratio of these parameters follows a predictable scaling with the scattering length. Our findings indicate that the dipolar three-body parameter is substantially larger than that typical of short-range interactions, yet it remains comparable in magnitude when expressed in units of two-body scattering length $a_2$. We also analyze the role of the dipolar angle and demonstrate that, even under short-range approximation conditions, the three-body parameter increases markedly as the angle approaches $54.7^{\circ}$, the magic angle.

arpov2020}, this article introduces a novel algorithm for computing the Hausdorff distance between polyhedral surfaces. The original method described therein relies on calculating the Hausdorff distance through the union of the shortest path geometries (OGS) of these surfaces, while this current approach determines the distance directly from the OGS structures themselves. Although the overall computational complexity remains constant at the cubic level, the algorithm achieves a significant enhancement in the average case by eliminating the reliance on costly general triangle intersection checks. This improvement arises by substituting such operations with more efficient calculations specific to tetrahedrons and the geometric properties of their associated triangular faces.

This challenge stems from the complex nature of multi-stage, multi-armed randomised controlled trials (RCTs) and their extensive configuration settings. In this study, the authors demonstrate that employing pattern-mixture mixture models for a within-study, conditional power analysis offers an effective means to assess such trials. The proposed methodology enables researchers to simulate various trial configuration scenarios using actual data from existing trials. Furthermore, it permits the conditional assessment of primary endpoints across multiple group comparisons and allows for cross-endpoint evaluations within a single study context. The methodology is illustrated using data from the evaluation of emergency department workflows for adult patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome, covering multiple RCTs conducted at the same institution.

However, this process remains difficult due to extensive pose variability and the subtle homogeneity between adjacent vertebrae. To address this, this paper introduces a novel instance segmentation framework that leverages shape and appearance cues. The method employs a Vision Transformer to capture long-range dependencies, facilitating identification, segmentation, and localization. By utilizing soft attention maps derived from the Vision Transformer, coarse class localization is achieved and fed to the localization branch of a Siamese Fully Convolutional Instance Segmentation Network (FCIS). A siamese architecture is employed to enhance the model's ability to learn from scarce data and boost generalization, with siamese weights combined at the end of the deep networks. The soft attention maps further serve as an input to a second branch of the siamese network to obtain detailed per-instance localization. Finally, these detailed localization outputs and attention maps are utilized by a segmentation branch of the siamese network, initialized with labels extracted from the previous two branches. Experiments demonstrate that this approach, trained only on a limited dataset of 200 CT scans, achieves state-of-the-art performance, attaining a mIoU of 73.6\%.

This approach builds upon the nearest separable state (NSS) problem, which itself extends further into finding the nearest fully separable state (NFS). We outline variational algorithms for both N SS and NFS, enhancing them with annealing techniques and proving that these annealed versions reach the globally optimal solution. We further analyze the performance differences between the algorithms applied to the CSS versus the NFS problems and evaluate them across various test cases consisting of noisy qubit states, pure entangled states, and mixed entangled states. Software-defined radio and control offer a promising solution by dynamically adjusting system parameters in response to changing user needs. This paper introduces a novel framework for automating Wi-Fi optimization, leveraging our finding that performance variations across clients are primarily driven by shifts in spatial channel properties. To achieve this, we developed Wi-FiSteer, an open-source tool that uses real-time monitoring of channel characteristics to automatically optimize key rates for connected devices.
